stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $T\to T'$ be a first-order thickening of algebraic spaces and $X'$ an algebraic space over $T'$. Set $X=X'\times_{T'}T$ and let $i:X\to X'$ denote the base-change immersion. Suppose $\mathcal{F}'$ is an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module flat over $T'$ and set $\mathcal{F}=i^*\mathcal{F}'$. The following four conditions are equivalent: (1) $\mathcal{F}'$ is quasi-coherent of finite presentation; (2) $\mathcal{F}'$ is of finite presentation; (3) $\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent of finite presentation; (4) $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation.
hypotheses: Consider a cartesian square $X\to X'$ over $T\to T'$ of algebraic spaces, with $T\to T'$ a first-order thickening. Let $\mathcal{F}'$ be an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module flat over $T'$, and put $\mathcal{F}=i^*\mathcal{F}'$.
conclusions: $\mathcal{F}'$ is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation on $X'$.
$\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation on $X$.

reason: The proof identifies finite presentation with quasi-coherence and invokes Deformation Theory's finitely-presented module deformation lemma for the first-order thickening equivalence.
